title: How do we group four thousand into powers of sixty?
description: Four thousand is grouped into the landmark numbers of the Mesopotamian base sixty system, largest first. Keeko's doubt is that four thousand can be written as sixty six sixties and forty.
teaching_notes: One idea: take the biggest landmark that fits, then the next, and no count may reach sixty. Watch for students who let a count reach sixty or more.

source: Group 4000 into powers of 60 and say how it is written in base 60 with our own symbols.
video_script.why: The child groups a number into the landmarks one, sixty and three thousand six hundred, taking the biggest landmark first, as the Mesopotamian system does.
video_script.substitution: Take as many of the biggest landmark as fit, then of the next one, and keep every count below sixty.
video_script.anchor: the book's Mesopotamian landmarks one, sixty and three thousand six hundred, with our own symbols for them
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko writes four thousand as sixty six sixties and forty; the value is right, but a count may not reach sixty, so sixty of the sixties group into one three thousand six hundred
video_script.payoff_line: Four thousand is one lot of three thousand six hundred, six lots of sixty, and forty.

final_answer.spoken: four thousand is one lot of three thousand six hundred, six lots of sixty, and forty

maths_rules: landmarks of base 60: 1, 60, 60 x 60 = 3600, 60 x 3600 = 216000; 216000 is far too big for 4000
six 60s fit in 400: 6 x 60 = 360, and 400 - 360 = 40; 40 is less than 60
Keeko's slip: 66 x 60 = 3960 and 3960 + 40 = 4000 has the right value, but 66 is 60 or more, so 60 of the 60s make one 3600, leaving 6 sixties
video_script.design: One idea: take the biggest landmark that fits, then the next. The three landmarks stay in a row on the board while the leftover shrinks below each step.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the number system of ancient Mesopotamia.
<bookmark mark='sym'/>Its landmark numbers are one, sixty and three thousand six hundred.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>We must group four thousand using these landmarks, and then say how it is written. How many of each landmark do we need?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board with the empty box

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: sixty ones slide into one 60; sixty 60s slide into one 3600; sixty 3600s slide into one 216000; a clock face with 60 minutes in an hour

marks.climb: sixty of each landmark slide into the next landmark
marks.base: the words base sixty system appear under the row
marks.clock: a clock face shows 60 minutes in an hour

narration: <bookmark mark='climb'/>Each landmark is sixty times the one before. We get one, sixty, three thousand six hundred, and then two hundred sixteen thousand.
<bookmark mark='base'/>When every landmark is sixty times the one before, we call it a base sixty system.
<bookmark mark='clock'/>Our clocks still use sixty, with sixty minutes in an hour.

marks.given: 4000 and the landmarks 1, 60 and 3600 are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the number four thousand, and the landmarks one, sixty and three thousand six hundred.

beats.on_screen: To find: 4000 in landmarks, and how it is written with our symbols

marks.find: the words 4000 in landmarks and how it is written are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to group four thousand into landmarks, and then write it with our own symbols.

beats.on_screen: landmarks 1, 60, 3600; the next, 216000, is far too big for 4000

marks.big: 216000 is crossed out as too big

narration: <bookmark mark='list'/>Step one, list the landmarks we can use. They are one, sixty and three thousand six hundred.
<bookmark mark='big'/>The next landmark is two hundred sixteen thousand, which is far too big for four thousand.
<bookmark mark='fit'/>Step two, see how many three thousand six hundreds fit in four thousand. Only one fits.
<bookmark mark='left'/>Four thousand take away three thousand six hundred leaves four hundred.

beats.on_screen: six 60s fit in 400: 6 x 60 = 360; 400 - 360 = 40, which is less than 60

marks.sixties: six 60s are taken out of 400 and 6 x 60 = 360 is written
marks.rest: 400 - 360 = 40 is written and 40 is ticked as less than 60

narration: <bookmark mark='sixties'/>Step three, see how many sixties fit in four hundred. Six sixties make three hundred sixty.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>Four hundred take away three hundred sixty leaves forty, and forty is less than sixty.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, check by adding the parts. Three thousand six hundred, three hundred sixty and forty make four thousand.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 4000 = (1) × 3600 + (6) × 60 + 40; our symbols: 1 with the 3600 symbol, 6 with the 60 symbol, then 40

marks.write: the number is written as 1 with the 3600 symbol, 6 with the 60 symbol, then 40

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Four thousand is one lot of three thousand six hundred, six lots of sixty, and forty.
<bookmark mark='write'/>With our symbols, we write one with the three thousand six hundred symbol. Then comes six with the sixty symbol, and then forty.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the finished grouping
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's grouping 66 x 60 + 40 with the label 3960 + 40 = 4000; the count 66 is circled; sixty of the 60s slide into one 3600

marks.value: 3960 + 40 = 4000 is written and the count 66 is circled
marks.fix: sixty of the 60s slide into one 3600, leaving six 60s

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks four thousand is sixty six sixties and forty, with no three thousand six hundred at all.
<bookmark mark='value'/>The value works, since sixty six sixties are three thousand nine hundred sixty. But sixty six is a count of sixty or more.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Sixty sixties make one three thousand six hundred, so we group them. That leaves one of those and six sixties.
